headline: Last session: Sensex recovered 300 points, but markets logged a seventh consecutive weekly decline amid oil price volatility.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 28 September.

why: Recovery in the last session was supported by gains in the auto and consumer durables sectors.
Earlier heavy losses were triggered by crude oil prices surging above $100 per barrel.
Proposed insurance curbs and global economic uncertainty weighed on investor sentiment throughout the week.
Large public sector banks sold US dollars to help the rupee recover from its lows.
whatHappening: The Sensex and Nifty recorded their seventh consecutive weekly decline despite a late-week recovery.
TCS reported a 14% drop in net profit to ₹10,720 crore due to legal and labour costs.
India's forex reserves dropped to $781 billion after previously hitting a record peak.
Anmol Industries has filed for an IPO worth $188 million to raise capital.
summary: On the last trading day, Indian markets recovered some losses, though the Sensex and Nifty still posted a seventh straight weekly decline. TCS saw a significant profit drop, while broader markets were impacted by high oil prices and a reduction in forex reserves. The market is currently closed for the weekend and is scheduled to reopen on Monday, September 28.
